trails.title: Periodic Report
trails.description: Every day, thousands of documents pass through the headquarters. And this is merely one of them.

content.text:
Report Number: XXXXXXXXXXXXX

From: Field Investigation Team Leader Andreas Sylvester

To: Office of the Vice President, St. Pavlov Foundation

Dear Madam Vice President,

After a month of surveillance, my team has identified several Manus Vindictae agents operating in the southern United States. At least three have been traveling between Dallas, Austin, and Houston; they are likely establishing information and supply channels for the Order of Enlightenment. Several others are active along Route 77, frequently using aliases and disguise potions to keep their exact identities and numbers hidden; however, at least five false identities have been confirmed. Please find detailed information on these agents attached to this report.

I believe these findings further substantiate our hypothesis that the Order of Enlightenment is planning to carry out an unprecedented arcane ritual.

Additionally, informant reports indicate that a spy known as "Ms. Grace" is active in Texas (see attached document). We await your directive on whether to pursue further surveillance of this individual.

May the peace be with us.
    
Field Investigation Team Leader Andreas Sylvester



Reply:

To the Field Investigation Team,

Thank you for your diligent efforts in the pursuit of peace. The aforementioned intelligence has been documented.

Regarding "Ms. Grace," I am fully aware of the situation. Given the unknown intentions of this spy, I recommend a strategy of non-interference. Allow her to proceed in her actions for further observation.

May the peace be with us.

Vice President Constantine of the St. Pavlov Foundation

items.text: Armament Factory, Chisos
The empty factory is cold and damp.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Hah, let's see what you've got in there for me.
She wanders the factory, eventually spotting a large crate covered in postage stamps in the receiving room.
The crate is nailed tightly shut. She squints, having only the moonlight to help her read the words on the box.
Red 38, Lilya.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Hey, buddy!
She squats down and inspects the crate. After tapping it a few times, she frowns.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: They just left her in a wooden box. What kind of safekeeping is this?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Anyway, I don't have much time. I'll settle that with them later.
She grabs the crate and tries to lift it.
It doesn't budge—it's bound by arcanum.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Alright. At least they bothered to put a gravity ritual on it.
Light footsteps echo behind her.
Are you also preparing to evacuate?
Lilya turns around. A slender girl stands before her, a basket in her arms.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Ah, perfect timing. Are you in charge here?
The girl looks her up and down before giving a sweet smile.

items.speaker: Kayla
items.text: No, I'm not in charge of anything, Lieutenant. I'm just passing through. I'm Kayla, by the way.

items.speaker: Kayla
items.text: I heard some rattling here and thought some of those kids might've come back to steal weapons again. These things aren't cheap, and the kids know it.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Kids stealing from the military? Hah, that's a new one. Where are the guards here?

items.speaker: Kayla
items.text: Oh. Didn't they tell you, Lieutenant?
The girl sounds surprised.

items.speaker: Kayla
items.text: The army stationed here started evacuating a month ago. There aren't many of them around these days.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Evacuating?
The Foundation's report was correct. Lilya senses impending danger.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Then where can I find the soldiers that are still here?

items.speaker: Kayla
items.text: Hmm. You're new in town, right? Did you see a bar on your way here?

items.speaker: Kayla
items.text: That's where the Zeno soldiers spend their nights drinking. You might wanna check there first. That's probably where you'll find him.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Him? What does he look like?

items.speaker: Kayla
items.text: Like every other Zeno soldier. They all look the same to me. You'll know when you see him.
She pauses, looking the pilot up and down.

items.speaker: Kayla
items.text: But I have to tell you: The bar doesn't like outsiders. Have you heard of the Order of Enlightenment?

items.speaker: Kayla
items.text: It's an occult society—very active these days. They were preaching in this town just a few days ago. Today is their day of prayer.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: And, what does that have to do with me?

items.speaker: Kayla
items.text: The bar you're going to is where they gather to pray.

items.speaker: Kayla
items.text: That's all I know. If you're going up there, please be careful.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Hah. Thanks.
Lilya turns and leaves. The girl watches her as she goes.

items.speaker: Kayla
items.text: May the Sufferer watch over you.

items.speaker: Kayla
items.text: Great Sufferer, by your decree, the glory of former days shall grace our present path.
She whispers a prayer. As she clasps her hands together, the black facets of her ring shimmer.
Bar, Chisos

items.speaker: Guest I
items.text: Great Sufferer, by your decree, the glory of former days shall grace our present path.

items.speaker: Guest II
items.text: We dedicate our souls and minds to you. We seek the well-being of our people in your name.
A solemn atmosphere fills the bar. A small group has gathered under the dim lights, some in black robes, others in everyday clothes. They lean on each other like brothers and sisters.
The man leading the prayer raises his glass and gives a toast.

items.speaker: Bar Owner
items.text: May the Sufferer watch over you.

items.speaker: Bar Owner
items.text: Under THEIR grace, may our cups overflow.

items.speaker: Bar Owner
items.text: To the Sufferer.

items.speaker: Crowd
items.text: To the Sufferer!
The bar door flings open.

items.speaker: Guest I
items.text: Hm? Odd time for a stranger to come.
The young pilot looks around.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Not crashing the party, am I?
She heads straight to the bar, where the shelves glitter with various bottles.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Napa Valley, Californian red, Kentucky whiskey ... Hah, there's a lot of good stuff here.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: One vodka. Straight. The best you got.

items.speaker: Bar Owner
items.text: It ain't business hours, lady.
*click*
She knows that sound—someone's cocking a gun just inches away from her.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Hey, all I did was ask for a drink! Is this how you treat your customers?

items.speaker: Bar Owner
items.text: As I said, we ain't serving you.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Why? Don't you have vodka?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Fine, I can settle for whiskey. Have to learn to take what we can get, eh?

items.speaker: Bar Owner
items.text: You ain't getting that, either.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Seriously? You don't have any whiskey?
She glances at the whiskey bottles lining the shelves.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Pft. I'm starting to understand why Zeno evacuated. What's the point of living in a town where there's no real liquor? Especially for those drunkards.

items.speaker: Bar Owner
items.text: What's a Zeno lieutenant doing here, anyway? No alcohol fuel in that warehouse of yours?
The patrons laugh.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Hah! You sure have some interesting drinking habits down here.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: But I'm curious. What did this Sufferer promise you to make you all change your faith?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: I mean, that's quite an achievement, especially here in Texas.
She turns, narrowly avoiding a bullet. It whizzes past her hair.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Oh, so we're doing this now, are we?
Bottles crash to the floor, splashing alcohol all over the bar.

items.speaker: Bar Owner
items.text: *pant*

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Look, I don't care what you're doing here. Just tell me where that Zeno soldier went.
She looks down at the bar owner slumped over the counter.

items.speaker: Bar Owner
items.text: What Zeno soldier?
The man strains to open his swollen eyes.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Don't play dumb with me.

items.speaker: Bar Owner
items.text: Oh. That soldier. He's a complete idiot, that one.

items.speaker: Bar Owner
items.text: It's obvious that Zeno's abandoned him. But he insists that they left him here because they believed that only he could keep the warehouse safe.

items.speaker: Bar Owner
items.text: Why are you looking for him now if you decided to ditch him in the first place?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Listen, I can tell you guys aren't the biggest fans of Zeno, but that has nothing to do with me.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: I'm just here to get my stuff back.

items.speaker: Bar Owner
items.text: *exhale*
He takes a labored breath.

items.speaker: Bar Owner
items.text: Fine. If you insist on finding him, try your luck on the outskirts of town. He might be drinking there.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Hmph. Thanks.
She steps over the unconscious man beside her and leaves the bar.
